neighbours.label: describing how a human community is composed or lives: 'a group of people', 'a council of elders', 'working in their own homes'; the same words about objects stay quiet
fire: A jury is a group of citizens chosen to hear a trial.
The guild was governed by a board of master masons and merchants.
A clan is a body of families who trace their roots to one ancestor.
Many of the potters, mostly widows, work in their own courtyards using old methods.
The militia marched in close ranks of trained villagers armed with pikes.
Aristocracy places authority with a small circle of nobles defined by birth and land.
About a third of the tailors in the town stitch clothes in their own houses.
The synod was made up of bishops, and a panel of elders who settled disputes.
quiet: A galaxy is a group of stars held together by gravity.
The engine was fitted with a row of steel valves and pistons.
A playlist is a set of songs that share one theme.
Many of the pots, mostly old, sit on a shelf in the back room.
The parade float carried tight rows of paper flowers and lights.
Photosynthesis uses a small range of wavelengths defined by the pigment.
About a third of the rainfall in the town drains into its own reservoir.
She fixed her own bike, and she then bought a pack of new tires.

notes: The + pole leans toward biological populations (' population' is promoted); this pole may be the social side of that.
